# CANDIDATE-002: libssh leaves a stray-NEWKEYS session in an error state with an open socket

Status: confirmed local conformance observation; provisional informational / low severity.
Investigated on 2026-11-07 against existing Docker targets published only on 127.0.0.1.
Downloaded source was inspected only, never built or executed.

## Observation

After initial key exchange, a stray SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS makes libssh 0.12.2 stop processing that connection.
It neither replies nor immediately closes TCP.
Correct password authentication subsequently produces no reply, regardless of strict KEX or a client sequence reset.
This is a terminal session error left open by the target application's event loop, not installation of empty keys, a key exchange waiting for completion, or evidence of a whole-server hang.

The original `results/seqnr/*.txt` cover twelve implementations/configurations.
For bare NEWKEYS, libssh is silent in all variants; russh continues with the original transport state; OpenSSH continues with a strict-mode receive-counter reset; the remaining targets close.
The “pre-auth refused rekey” row must be interpreted separately: the preceding inputs can constitute a real rekey or fail earlier, so its final NEWKEYS is not uniformly a stray message across implementations.
The bare pre-auth and post-auth rows isolate this observation.

## Local experiments and exact outputs

Reproduction command: `uv run python scripts/stray_newkeys_followup.py`.
The new script uses the unchanged mapper and testbed, AES-128-CTR / HMAC-SHA2-256, and only the existing libssh Docker image.
Each NEWKEYS and immediate authentication/channel probe waits five seconds.
Variants A/B/C mean strict with retained counter, non-strict with retained counter, and strict with outgoing counter reset respectively.
Four affected sessions remain open together while a fifth connection completes authentication and opens a channel.
Raw output is preserved in [libssh-followup.txt](../results/seqnr/libssh-followup.txt).

## Tagged source and root cause

Source archives are stored under the requested scratch directory `codex-libssh-russh-src`.
The GitHub tag `libssh-0.12.2` resolves through annotated tag object `2d3aa9b36ab543049ca002c5b85c310ac328469b` to commit `07430deb9b97b751ec5ea5a7fc307f40bf042e0a`.
The russh `v0.65.1` tag resolves to `b33092aad1e51c66258a12e8b83fc473a68d9d34`.
SHA-256 of the downloaded codeload archives:

```text
92fef8a348070a6786667ed724d5e808d2530464bac37559a8d59c70ab1f1a83  libssh.tar.gz
fedda194924e6ec1c24f3247dfe8aab2c88c26db3e54a961318e9987297de655  russh.tar.gz
```

All libssh file:line references below refer to that tag.
[packet.c:68](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L68) registers `ssh_packet_newkeys` in the default callback table.
However, [packet.c:326–351](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L326) first filters NEWKEYS:

```c
if (session->session_state != SSH_SESSION_STATE_DH) {
    rc = SSH_PACKET_DENIED;
    break;
}
```

It additionally requires `dh_handshake_state == DH_STATE_NEWKEYS_SENT`.
After initial KEX, the bare message fails the session-state requirement.
[packet.c:1575–1588](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1575) executes callbacks only for allowed packets.
The denied branch records `Packet filter: rejected packet (type %d)` with `SSH_FATAL` and jumps to `error`.
[packet.c:1626–1629](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1626) then does:

```c
session->session_state = SSH_SESSION_STATE_ERROR;
SSH_LOG(SSH_LOG_PACKET, "Packet: processed %zu bytes", processed);
return processed;
```

This branch does not send DISCONNECT, close the socket, or clear `alive`.
On subsequent input, [packet.c:1309–1311](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1309) tests the error state and jumps straight to the same error return, before packet decryption.
The socket callback at [socket.c:377–385](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/socket.c#L377) consumes only the returned byte count and stops retrying when that count is zero.
This explains silence without an immediate busy loop; further incoming bytes may remain buffered instead of being processed.
No memory-growth stress experiment was performed.

Even if reached directly, [packet_cb.c:155–162](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet_cb.c#L155) repeats the same session/DH checks and errors before the strict receive-counter reset at lines 164–166.
Its error path at lines 280–288 also sets the session error state.
Thus this observation is not the OpenSSH reset-before-dispatch behavior from CANDIDATE-001.

Neither filter failure nor callback state-check failure touches `next_crypto` or `current_crypto`.
The real key-switch routine, [packet.c:2165–2220](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L2165), marks directional use of `next_crypto`, retires current directional use, and promotes `next_crypto` only once both directions have switched.
It then allocates a fresh pending crypto object and copies the session ID into it.
That pending object existing after KEX does not mean it becomes active on a stray NEWKEYS: this error path never calls `ssh_packet_set_newkeys()`.
The existing current crypto remains installed, but the session error gate prevents using it for later packets.
The authenticated but rejected stray packet itself increments the receive counter in the normal packet path at packet.c:1538; no strict reset occurs.

## Per-connection versus whole-server impact

`targets/libssh/server.c` creates a detached thread per accepted connection.
After `ssh_handle_key_exchange()`, its thread loops on `ssh_is_connected(s)` and calls `ssh_event_dopoll(event, 1000)`, breaking only on `SSH_ERROR`.
[session.c:712–718](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/session.c#L712) implements connection status as `return session->alive;`, without checking `session_state`.
[Poll handling at poll.c:743–748](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/poll.c#L743) returns `SSH_AGAIN` on an idle timeout.
Consequently the application can keep polling an errored but still alive socket.
The application prints `ssh_get_error()` only after leaving that loop.
In this run the later socket-disconnection error was what appeared in those logs; the original filter error was not preserved there.
Applications which explicitly detect terminal session errors and disconnect may have a different lifetime.

The successful parallel connection proves the listener and other connection threads remain functional with four affected connections present.
The CPU and closure observations are bounded measurements reported above, not a claim of unlimited resource exhaustion.

## Short comparison: russh 0.65.1

In [server/mod.rs:1206](https://github.com/Eugeny/russh/blob/v0.65.1/russh/src/server/mod.rs#L1206), `reply()` classifies key-exchange messages with `is_kex_msg`.
[msg.rs:165–170](https://github.com/Eugeny/russh/blob/v0.65.1/russh/src/msg.rs#L165) includes NEWKEYS in that set.
[server/mod.rs:1240–1242](https://github.com/Eugeny/russh/blob/v0.65.1/russh/src/server/mod.rs#L1240) only passes such packets to the KEX machine if the session is `SessionKexState::InProgress`.
After KEX completes it sets the state to Idle at line 1295.
An idle stray NEWKEYS therefore falls through to `session.server_read_encrypted(handler, pkt).await` at line 1312.

[server/encrypted.rs:35–41](https://github.com/Eugeny/russh/blob/v0.65.1/russh/src/server/encrypted.rs#L35) forwards to `process_packet()`.
During authentication, its state/message match has no NEWKEYS arm and ends at line 161 with `_ => Ok(())`.
After authentication, lines 150–159 route to `server_read_authenticated()`; its final arm at lines 2020–2023 is:

```rust
m => {
    debug!("unknown message received: {m:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

This is the no-op which accounts for silence and continued use of existing crypto.
Key installation and strict sequence reset occur only in the real KEX completion branch, server/mod.rs:1255–1300.
“Unchanged sequence numbers” here means no reset: normal packet-number advancement still occurs when the stray packet is read.
Variant A continuing while C closes is consistent with that distinction.
There is no demonstrated key replacement, sequence rollback, authentication bypass, or session availability loss in russh's bare-message path.

## Severity and confidence

Assessment: **informational / low**, with high confidence in the libssh state transition and russh no-op, and moderate confidence in deployment impact.
A peer can trigger libssh's state error before user authentication, after completing transport KEX.
A fresh valid encrypted stray NEWKEYS requires that peer's transport keys; this does not establish a trigger available to an on-path attacker between honest endpoints.
The local result is loss of progress on the sending peer's own session and retained connection/thread resources until cleanup.
An idle client already retains resources in this target; the experiment does not establish an amplification factor or a distinct whole-server denial of service.
There is no observed CPU spin, crash, authentication bypass, plaintext disclosure, or switch to uninitialised cryptography.
The library's terminal error and the embedding application's cleanup policy must be considered together before assigning broader availability impact.

## Summary

libssh rejects out-of-KEX NEWKEYS, enters a terminal session error before key switching, and this target keeps polling the open connection.
Other connections still work.
russh silently ignores the message outside active KEX and continues with existing keys and normally advancing counters.
"""Replay input words on a real target and print outputs and the packet trace.

    uv run python scripts/replay.py <target> "KEXINIT KEX30 NEWKEYS ..." ["..."] [--reps N] [--trace]
"""
import sys
from smlearn import testbed
from smlearn.ssh.mapper import SSHMapper

args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
reps = int(next((a.split("=")[1] for a in sys.argv if a.startswith("--reps=")), 3))
show_trace = "--trace" in sys.argv
target = testbed.load_target(args[0])
testbed.build(target)
inst = testbed.start(target)
try:
    m = SSHMapper(inst.host, inst.port, user=target.user, password=target.password, timeout=0.8, quiet=0.2)
    for word in args[1:]:
        word = word.split()
        runs = []
        for _ in range(reps):
            m.reset()
            runs.append([m.step(i) for i in word])
        print(f"\n{target.name}: {' '.join(word)}")
        print(f"  deterministic over {reps}: {all(r == runs[0] for r in runs)}")
        for i, o in zip(word, runs[0]):
            print(f"  {i:16} -> {o}")
        if show_trace:
            for d, n, h in m.trace:
                print(f"    {d} {n:18} {h[:80]}")
    m.close()
finally:
    inst.stop()

    'KEXINIT', 'KEX30', 'NEWKEYS', 'SR_AUTH', 'SR_CONN', 'UA_PW_OK', 'UA_PW_NOK', 'UA_NONE',
    'CH_OPEN', 'CH_CLOSE', 'CH_EOF', 'CH_DATA', 'CH_REQUEST_EXEC',
    'IGNORE', 'DEBUG', 'UNIMPLEMENTED', 'DISCONNECT',
)
NAMES = dict(zip(
    (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 20, 21, 30, 31, 51, 52, 53, 80, 81, 82,
     91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100),
    ('DISCONNECT', 'IGNORE', 'UNIMPLEMENTED', 'DEBUG', 'SERVICE_ACCEPT', 'EXT_INFO',
     'KEXINIT', 'NEWKEYS', 'KEX30', 'KEX31', 'UA_FAILURE', 'UA_SUCCESS', 'UA_BANNER',
     'GLOBAL_REQUEST', 'REQUEST_SUCCESS', 'REQUEST_FAILURE', 'CH_OPEN_SUCCESS',
     'CH_OPEN_FAILURE', 'CH_WINDOW_ADJUST', 'CH_DATA', 'CH_EXTENDED_DATA', 'CH_EOF',
     'CH_CLOSE', 'CH_REQUEST', 'CH_SUCCESS', 'CH_FAILURE')))
NAMES.update({5: 'SERVICE_REQUEST', 50: 'UA_REQUEST', 90: 'CH_OPEN'})
VERSION = b'SSH-2.0-smlearn_0.1'


class SSHMapper:
    def __init__(self, host, port, user='test', password='test', *, timeout=1.0,
                 quiet=0.15, strict_kex=True):
        self.host, self.port = host, port
        self.user, self.password = user, password
        self.timeout, self.quiet = timeout, quiet
        self.strict_kex = strict_kex
        self.sock = None
        self.trace = []
        self.strict_kex_active = False
        self.server_kex = None

    def close(self):
        if self.sock is not None:
            self.sock.close()
            self.sock = None

    def reset(self):
        self.close()
        self.trace = []
        self.incoming, self.outgoing = Direction(), Direction()
        self.buffer = bytearray()
        self.client_kex = self.server_kex = self.private_key = None
        self.pending = {}
        self.session_id = self.channel = None
        self.strict_kex_active = False
        self.sock = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port), self.timeout)
        self.sock.sendall(VERSION + b'\r\n')
        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.timeout
        while True:
            while b'\n' not in self.buffer:
                self.sock.settimeout(max(0.001, deadline - time.monotonic()))
                data = self.sock.recv(65536)
                if not data:
                    self.close()
                    raise EOFError('closed during SSH identification')
                self.buffer.extend(data)
            line, _, rest = self.buffer.partition(b'\n')
            self.buffer = bytearray(rest)
            if line.startswith(b'SSH-'):
                self.server_version = bytes(line).rstrip(b'\r')
                break
        self._collect(self.quiet)

    def _install(self, direction, outgoing):
        keys = self.pending.pop(outgoing, None)
        if keys is not None:
            direction.install(*keys)
            if self.strict_kex_active:
                direction.sequence = 0

    def _received(self, payload):
        kind = payload[0]
        fields = Reader(payload[1:])
        if kind == 20:
            if self.server_kex is None:
                # Strict KEX is negotiated once, by the initial server KEXINIT.
                fields.take(16)
                offered = fields.string().split(b',')
                self.strict_kex_active = self.strict_kex and b'kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com' in offered
            self.server_kex = payload
        elif kind == 31 and self.client_kex and self.server_kex and self.private_key:
            host_key, public = fields.string(), fields.string()
            fields.string()  # Host signature is deliberately not verified in this testbed.
            shared = self.private_key.exchange(X25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(public))
            secret = int.from_bytes(shared, 'big')
            transcript = (VERSION, self.server_version, self.client_kex, self.server_kex,
                          host_key, self.private_key.public_key().public_bytes_raw(), public)
            exchange_hash = hashlib.sha256(b''.join(string(x) for x in transcript) + mpint(secret)).digest()
            if self.session_id is None:
                self.session_id = exchange_hash
            a, b, c, d, e, f = derive_keys(secret, exchange_hash, self.session_id)
            self.pending = {True: (a, c, e), False: (b, d, f)}
        elif kind == 21:
            self._install(self.incoming, False)
        elif kind == 91:
            fields.uint32()
            self.channel = fields.uint32()
        elif kind == 97:
            self.channel = None

    def _collect(self, first_timeout):
        outputs = []
        deadline = time.monotonic() + first_timeout
        while self.sock is not None:
            try:
                payload = self.incoming.decode(self.buffer)
                if payload is not None:
                    if not payload:
                        raise BadPacket('empty payload')
                    name = NAMES.get(payload[0], f'MSG{payload[0]}')
                    self.trace.append(('<', name, payload.hex()))
                    self._received(payload)
                    if not outputs or outputs[-1] != name:
                        outputs.append(name)
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + self.quiet
                    continue
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    break
                self.sock.settimeout(remaining)
                data = self.sock.recv(65536)
                if not data:
                    self.close()
                    outputs.append('CLOSED')
                    break
                self.buffer.extend(data)
            except socket.timeout:
                break
            except OSError:
                self.close()
                outputs.append('CLOSED')
            except ValueError:
                self.close()
                outputs.append('BAD_PACKET')
        return '+'.join(outputs) if outputs else 'NO_RESP'

    def _payload(self, symbol):
        if symbol == 'KEXINIT':
            kex = 'curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org'
            if self.strict_kex:
                kex += ',kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com'
            lists = (kex, 'ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256,ecdsa-sha2-nistp256',
                     'aes128-ctr', 'aes128-ctr', 'hmac-sha2-256', 'hmac-sha2-256',
                     'none', 'none', '', '')
            self.client_kex = b'\x14' + bytes(16) + b''.join(string(x) for x in lists) + b'\0' + uint32(0)
            return self.client_kex
        if symbol == 'KEX30':
            self.private_key = X25519PrivateKey.generate()
            return b'\x1e' + string(self.private_key.public_key().public_bytes_raw())
        if symbol == 'NEWKEYS':
            return b'\x15'
        if symbol in ('SR_AUTH', 'SR_CONN'):
            return b'\x05' + string('ssh-userauth' if symbol == 'SR_AUTH' else 'ssh-connection')
        if symbol.startswith('UA_'):
            payload = b'\x32' + string(self.user) + string('ssh-connection')
            if symbol == 'UA_NONE':
                return payload + string('none')
            password = self.password if symbol == 'UA_PW_OK' else self.password + '-wrong'
            return payload + string('password') + b'\0' + string(password)
        if symbol == 'CH_OPEN':
            return b'\x5a' + string('session') + uint32(0) + uint32(2**21) + uint32(32768)
        if symbol.startswith('CH_'):
            channel = uint32(self.channel)
            return {
                'CH_CLOSE': b'\x61' + channel,
                'CH_EOF': b'\x60' + channel,
                'CH_DATA': b'\x5e' + channel + string(b'x'),
                'CH_REQUEST_EXEC': b'\x62' + channel + string('exec') + b'\x01' + string('true'),
            }[symbol]
        return {'IGNORE': b'\x02' + string(b''),
                'DEBUG': b'\x04\0' + string(b'') + string(b''),
                'UNIMPLEMENTED': b'\x03' + uint32(0),
                'DISCONNECT': b'\x01' + uint32(11) + string(b'') + string(b'')}[symbol]

    def step(self, symbol):
        if symbol not in INPUTS:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown SSH input: {symbol}')
        if self.sock is None:
            return 'NO_CONN'
        if symbol in ('CH_CLOSE', 'CH_EOF', 'CH_DATA', 'CH_REQUEST_EXEC') and self.channel is None:
            return 'NO_CHANNEL'
        payload = self._payload(symbol)
        try:
            self.sock.sendall(self.outgoing.encode(payload))
        except OSError:
            self.close()
            return 'CLOSED'
        self.trace.append(('>', NAMES.get(payload[0], f'MSG{payload[0]}'), payload.hex()))
        if symbol == 'NEWKEYS':
            self._install(self.outgoing, True)
        elif symbol == 'CH_CLOSE':
            self.channel = None
        return self._collect(self.timeout)
"""Start and stop target implementations as local Docker containers.

Every container publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 only, on a random host port,
so many instances of the same target can run side by side.
"""

import json
import socket
import subprocess
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

TARGETS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "targets"


@dataclass
class Target:
    name: str
    implementation: str
    source: str
    port: int
    user: str = "test"
    password: str = "test"

    @property
    def image(self) -> str:
        return f"smlearn-{self.name}"


def load_target(name: str) -> Target:
    data = json.loads((TARGETS_DIR / name / "target.json").read_text())
    return Target(**{k: data[k] for k in Target.__dataclass_fields__ if k in data})


def list_targets() -> list[str]:
    return sorted(p.parent.name for p in TARGETS_DIR.glob("*/target.json"))


def build(target: Target) -> None:
    subprocess.run(["docker", "build", "-q", "-t", target.image, str(TARGETS_DIR / target.name)],
                   check=True, capture_output=True)


@dataclass
class Instance:
    target: Target
    container_id: str
    host: str
    port: int

    def stop(self) -> None:
        subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", self.container_id], capture_output=True)

    def logs(self) -> str:
        r = subprocess.run(["docker", "logs", self.container_id], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.stdout + r.stderr


def start(target: Target, ready_timeout: float = 30.0) -> Instance:
    """Run one container and wait until it sends an SSH identification line."""
    cid = subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "run", "-d", "--rm", "--label", "smlearn=1",
         "-p", f"127.0.0.1::{target.port}", target.image],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    out = subprocess.run(["docker", "port", cid, f"{target.port}/tcp"],
                         check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    host_port = int(out.splitlines()[0].rsplit(":", 1)[1])
    inst = Instance(target, cid, "127.0.0.1", host_port)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + ready_timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            with socket.create_connection((inst.host, inst.port), timeout=2) as s:
                if s.recv(256).startswith(b"SSH-"):
                    return inst
        except OSError:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.3)
    logs = inst.logs()
    inst.stop()
    raise RuntimeError(f"{target.name} did not become ready:\n{logs}")

### Messages a party may send inside a key exchange (`KEX-SERVER-SENDS-NON-KEX`, `KEXINIT-DUPLICATE`, `SR-ACCEPT-BEFORE-NEWKEYS`)

RFC 4253 §7.1, MUST NOT:

> Once a party has sent a SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message for key exchange or re-exchange, until it has sent a SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS message (Section 7.3), it MUST NOT send any messages other than:
>
> o Transport layer generic messages (1 to 19) (but SSH_MSG_SERVICE_REQUEST and SSH_MSG_SERVICE_ACCEPT MUST NOT be sent);
>
> o Algorithm negotiation messages (20 to 29) (but further SSH_MSG_KEXINIT messages MUST NOT be sent);
>
> o Specific key exchange method messages (30 to 49).

> Note, however, that during a key re-exchange, after sending a SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message, each party MUST be prepared to process an arbitrary number of messages that may be in-flight before receiving a SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message from the other party.

This constrains the sender.
The server has sent its KEXINIT before the mapper's first step,
so until it sends NEWKEYS it must not send SERVICE_ACCEPT, KEXINIT, or any message numbered 50 or higher.

RFC 4253 §7.3:

> Key exchange ends by each side sending an SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS message.

> All messages sent after this message MUST use the new keys and algorithms.

### Service request after the key exchange (`SR-ACCEPT-BEFORE-NEWKEYS`)

RFC 4253 §10, descriptive (no keyword):

> After the key exchange, the client requests a service.

RFC 4253 §10, MUST:

> If the server rejects the service request, it SHOULD send an appropriate SSH_MSG_DISCONNECT message and MUST disconnect.

> If the server supports the service (and permits the client to use it), it MUST respond with the following:

RFC 4251 §1, descriptive:

> The client sends a service request once a secure transport layer connection has been established.

> A second service request is sent after user authentication is complete.

Before the server NEWKEYS, a SERVICE_ACCEPT breaks the §7.1 MUST NOT.
Between the server NEWKEYS and the client NEWKEYS the RFCs only describe the order,
so accepting there is a MUST violation only because strict KEX is active.
The §10 rule "reject means disconnect" is not encoded on its own:
servers commonly answer a repeated SERVICE_REQUEST with UNIMPLEMENTED,
and it is unclear whether such a message counts as a service request or as an unexpected message (§11.4).

### Key re-exchange (`REKEY-KEXINIT-REPLY`, `KEXINIT-DUPLICATE`)

### AsyncSSH rogue extension negotiation and rogue session (CVE-2023-46445, CVE-2023-46446)

- Rogue extension negotiation (client side): the AsyncSSH client accepted an `EXT_INFO` injected in plaintext before the key exchange completed; prefix truncation then deletes the real one ([Terrapin, §6.1, Fig. 6](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity24-baumer.pdf), [GHSA-cfc2-wr2v-gxm5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfc2-wr2v-gxm5)).
  It affects AsyncSSH < 2.14.1.
- Rogue session (server side): the AsyncSSH server accepted a `USERAUTH_REQUEST` injected before the client's NEWKEYS, and "defers it until the client has requested the authentication protocol" ([Terrapin, §6.2, Fig. 7](https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity24-baumer.pdf), [GHSA-c35q-ffpf-5qpm](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c35q-ffpf-5qpm)).
  It then "silently ignores any additional authentication request after a successful authentication" (Terrapin, §6.2).
  This affects AsyncSSH < 2.14.1.
- The 2.14.1 fix makes messages above 49 before incoming encryption, KEX messages outside a KEX, and auth messages outside authentication into protocol errors.
  It also adds `_auth_final`: after the first message above 79, further auth requests disconnect instead of being ignored ([commit 83e43f5](https://github.com/ronf/asyncssh/commit/83e43f5ea3470a8617fc388c72b062c7136efd7e)).

## 4. Other SSH server state-machine bugs (protocol behaviour only)

- **libssh CVE-2018-10933** (0.6 to before 0.7.6/0.8.4): a client that sends `SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS` where the server expects `USERAUTH_REQUEST` gets the server's state machine set to authenticated, and can then create channels ([libssh advisory](https://www.libssh.org/security/advisories/CVE-2018-10933.txt)).
- **Paramiko CVE-2018-1000805**: the same class.
  The server dispatched a client-sent `MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS` to a handler meant for client use and marked the peer as authenticated ([paramiko#1283](https://github.com/paramiko/paramiko/issues/1283)).
- **Paramiko CVE-2018-7750**: the server did "not properly check whether authentication is completed before processing other requests, as demonstrated by channel-open" ([OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2018-7750)).
- **AsyncSSH CVE-2018-7749** (< 1.12.1): the same, "a customized SSH client can simply skip the authentication step" ([OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2018-7749)).
- **Erlang/OTP SSH CVE-2025-32433** (before OTP 27.3.3, 26.2.5.11, 25.3.2.20): `CHANNEL_OPEN` and `CHANNEL_REQUEST exec`, sent right after KEXINIT and before KEX_ECDH_INIT, are processed.
